title: Cap. VIII Arg. 1: Scripture — God does not will that men perish
pass_a_gloss: That reprobation therefore flows from the foresighted demerits of men, some first try to prove from those places of Scripture in which God is said by no means to will that men perish: Which would be least true, if God by his will alone, and not on account of sins, reprobated so great a multitude of men. Hither they bring that of Ezek. 18:23, Is the death of the wicked of my will? and Hos. 13:9. Thy destruction is from thee. Likewise that of the Apostle, 1 Tim. 2:4. God wills all to be made safe. And that of the Savior, Matt. 11:28. Come unto me all; and very many other places of that kind, which it is not necessary to repeat or discuss one by one.
pass_b_english: First they try to prove reprobation flows from foresighted human demerits from those Scripture places where God is said not to will that men perish — which would hardly be true, they say, if God by his will alone, and not for sins, reprobated so great a multitude. They cite Ezek. 18:23 (Is the death of the wicked of my will?), Hos. 13:9 (Your destruction is from you), 1 Tim. 2:4 (God wills all to be saved), Matt. 11:28 (Come to me, all), and many like places — no need to repeat or discuss them one by one.
source_text: Reprobationem igitur fluere ex praevisis hominum demeritis, primo probare conantur nonnulli ex illis Scripturae locis, in quibus Deus dicitur nequaquam velle ut homines pereant: Quod minime verum esset, si Deus sola sua voluntate, et non propter peccata, tantam hominum multitudinem reprobaret. Huc afferunt illud Ezek. xviii. 23, Nunquid voluntatis meae est mors impii? et Hos. xiii. 9. Perditio tua ex te. Item illud Apostoli, 1 Tim. ii. 4. Deus vult omnes salvos fieri. Et illud Servatoris, Matth. xi. 28. Venite ad me omnes; ejusque generis loca alia quamplurima, quae sigillatim repetere aut discutere non est necesse.
